features.name: Deterministic CPU particle billboard rendering
features.behavior: A fixed-seed CPU particle simulation publishes one immutable generation-qualified owned-value packet that survives Scene extraction without mutation, and the renderer performs stable per-view sorting, rotating-buffer upload, cached billboard batching, and native instanced draws with exact execution evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Two fresh particle instances advanced with the same fixed seed and ticks publish byte-identical immutable CPU packets, while later simulation cannot mutate an already published packet.

The owned-value packet crosses SceneFeatureSnapshotStore, FrozenSceneSnapshot, extraction, RenderSceneDatabase, and the Render feature boundary without mutation, content-hash rewriting, or producer-generation rewriting.
GFX16 supports CPU Billboard particles with AlphaBlend, Premultiplied, and Additive policies; unsupported modes, malformed payloads, and GPU-owned payloads fail closed.
Per-view depth sorting is stable, never mutates the source packet, and batches equal render policy into one Draw(6, instanceCount) call.
Render-owned frame resources rotate across safe frame slots; after warm-up pipeline, descriptor, and buffer counts stop growing and no WaitIdle call is used.
The particle billboard VS/PS is consumed through the cooked shader catalog, while raw particle shader copying and unimplemented simulation shader claims are removed.
DX12 and Vulkan native validation record executed graph pass, draw count, instance count, upload bytes, and zero fallback for the particle path.
Focused tests, full Windows Build Truth, DX12/Vulkan native coverage, Shipping closure, Architecture, and diff hygiene pass with current evidence.

features.name: Deterministic fire, smoke, soft particles, and distortion
features.behavior: Fixed-tick particle effects travel through a strict CookedParticleEffectArtifact, CookManifest, runtime loader, and Sample catalog before rendering cooked flipbook fire and premultiplied smoke through the GFX16 immutable packet path; they consume canonical scene depth for soft intersections, publish typed RG16F distortion and reactive-mask outputs, and composite without hidden fallback or Sample access to renderer internals. Scope expanded after read-only discovery proved that the existing Source-only placeholder ParticleSystemLoader and model-only Sample catalog could not satisfy the requested cooked-only runtime contract.
acceptanceCriteria: Fixed simulationTick, fixedDeltaSeconds, deterministic seed, and effect descriptor produce identical flipbook frame selection, particle attributes, content hashes, and optional light samples without reading wall clock.

Fire uses additive HDR-safe billboards and smoke uses premultiplied billboards; atlas layout, frame range, rate, UV transform, and texture identity are immutable cooked/runtime inputs rather than backend branches.

Soft particles consume a RenderGraph-owned frozen copy of the canonical D32 scene depth, reconstruct view-linear depth with the frame projection contract, and fade intersections monotonically; missing CopySrc support, incompatible extent/domain, or unsupported backend capability fails closed when required.

Distorting particles write a typed RG16F vector field and R8 reactive contribution, then a separate graph pass composites from an opaque/translucent snapshot without same-texture read/write hazards; zero distortion is an identity operation.
The optional low-frequency fire light is deterministic, bounded, explicitly reported, and never mutates World or renderer lighting state through an unowned pointer.

particle-fire and particle-smoke are backend-neutral cooked-only Sample scenarios with fixed cameras, ticks, manifests, readiness receipts, and no dependency on RHI, Render private headers, AssetImport, or ShaderCompiler.
DX12 and Vulkan execute fire and smoke on Forward+ and Deferred with cooked shaders, real image/report/startup evidence, zero renderer fallback, and exact particle/distortion/reactive-mask receipts.

features.name: Deterministic Gerstner water surfaces and gameplay queries
features.behavior: A versioned immutable Water render packet carries bounded canonical Gerstner waves and material parameters from ECS extraction without owning a second clock. Runtime gameplay queries and renderer shader evaluation share the same pure reference contract and consume the same explicit frozen EffectFrameTime, while Render owns the grid, displacement, layered normals, Fresnel reflection, depth thickness, Beer-Lambert absorption, foam, reactive-mask output, and graph ordering. The cooked-only backend-neutral water-surface Sample proves the same path on Forward+ and Deferred without Sample access to RHI or renderer internals.
acceptanceCriteria: A bounded canonical Gerstner wave set rejects zero directions and non-finite or out-of-policy amplitude, wavelength, steepness, speed, and count values, and produces a stable content hash without wall-clock or process-entropy input.

Runtime height, displacement, normal, tangent, horizontal velocity, and signed distance queries are pure functions of canonical parameters, world position, and explicit simulationSeconds; repeated fixed tick inputs are bit-stable within the documented floating-point contract.

The Water ECS gateway seals timeless immutable parameters and rejects stale generation, schema, sequence, source-version, or content-hash data; gameplay and rendering then consume the same explicit frozen EffectFrameTime so neither can observe a previous-frame or one-frame-ahead surface.

RenderWater depends only on RenderFoundation, RenderGraph, RenderContracts, RHI, and cooked shader contracts; it owns grid geometry and rotating GPU resources and never includes gameplay Water headers or performs WaitIdle, per-frame pipeline creation, or per-vertex CPU uploads.

Water executes after an opaque scene snapshot and before sorted translucency and particles, samples canonical depth for thickness, writes HDR scene color plus a reactive contribution without in-place read/write hazards, and reports its actual ordering and resource identities.

The shader implements Gerstner displacement, two deterministic normal layers, Schlick Fresnel, depth-derived thickness, Beer-Lambert absorption, bounded foam, and reflection fallback; zero waves and zero absorption have explicit identity behavior.

CPU reference points and shader/native probes agree within declared tolerances for displacement, normal, thickness, absorption, and foam, and Forward+ and Deferred use the same Water feature contract.
water-surface is a cooked-only backend-neutral Sample with a fixed camera, tick, manifest, readiness receipt, and no dependency on RHI, Render private headers, AssetImport, or ShaderCompiler.
DX12 and Vulkan execute water-surface on Forward+ and Deferred with cooked shaders, real image/report/startup evidence, zero renderer fallback, and exact water/reactive-mask receipts.

features.name: Local shadows, reflection probes, and Hi-Z reflections
features.behavior: Point and spot lights render through a deterministic local-shadow atlas, local reflection probes are selected and blended without global mutable state, and Hi-Z screen-space reflections expose confidence so every invalid or missed ray resolves explicitly through SSR to Probe to IBL instead of producing black output.
acceptanceCriteria: Point and spot shadow requests use a deterministic Render-owned atlas allocator with stable light identity, bounded capacity, generation-safe handles, explicit overflow diagnostics, and no per-frame pipeline or atlas recreation.
Local shadows share the clustered LightingFramePlan identity, preserve masked-material shadow silhouettes, and are consumed identically by Forward+ and Deferred lighting.

Reflection probes declare bounded influence volumes and priority, are selected and blended by a deterministic top-N policy, and cannot rely on process-global mutable state or backend-specific Sample logic.

Hi-Z is built from canonical depth with validated mip extents and reduction policy; SSR records hit validity, confidence, and rejection reason rather than treating an invalid sample as a valid black reflection.
Reflection resolution follows one explicit SSR to Probe to IBL chain, with each fallback declared by feature readiness and the execution receipt recording the path that actually executed.

features.name: Weighted blended order-independent translucency
features.behavior: Forward+ and Deferred share one immutable translucency plan that routes eligible non-refractive alpha and premultiplied mesh and particle draws through weighted blended OIT, preserves ThinTransmission on the strictly sorted refraction path and additive content on the direct path, and fails closed whenever requested independent FP16 attachment blending is unavailable or execution evidence is incomplete.
acceptanceCriteria: The public RHI reports independent color-attachment blending and per-format ColorAttachment and ColorAttachmentBlend support from backend-native queries; pipeline preflight rejects unsupported active render-target formats and blend rows before native object creation.

One immutable TranslucencyFramePlan routes every eligible mesh and particle draw exactly once: StandardLit or Unlit AlphaBlend and Premultiplied use WeightedBlended, ThinTransmission uses SortedRefraction, Additive uses DirectAdditive, and every unsupported combination has a structured reason.

Weighted blended accumulation uses graph-owned RGBA16_FLOAT accumulation cleared to zero and R16_FLOAT revealage cleared to one, with independent blend state, deterministic bounded weighting, and a fullscreen composite that updates scene-linear HDR and the reactive mask without sampling and writing the same texture.

Forward+ and Deferred consume the same translucency policy and execution path; OIT is recipe-neutral, the temporary resources remain feature-private, and the final typed TranslucencyOutputs identify the exact frame, view, plan, and graph generation.

ThinTransmission remains strictly back-to-front after OIT composite and consumes the immutable opaque scene snapshot; additive mesh and particle content remains direct and does not enter accumulation; particle upload and distortion execute at most once.

A requested Required OIT mode fails before graph execution when independent FP16 blending, shaders, pipelines, inputs, clears, draws, composite, or receipts are unavailable; an explicitly Optional mode may use only the declared sorted-translucency fallback and records that fallback.

DX12 and Vulkan native evidence proves independent RGBA16_FLOAT plus R16_FLOAT blending, mixed mesh and particle accumulation, composite execution, no fallback, and exact frame/view identity; Metal native evidence remains required in remote CI.
